edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a harmful direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.population: adults sleeping in poorly ventilated bedrooms
edges.mechanism: Poor overnight ventilation can raise bedroom CO2 enough to increase stuffiness, sleep fragmentation, and morning headache even without frank hypoxia.
edges.summary: The strongest piece here is the 2023 Klausen rct in Int J Occup Med Environ Health, which ties high bedroom co2 to sleep quality in a direction that later studies largely support. That makes this edge more about calibrating magnitude and context than arguing over whether the signal exists at all.
edges.caveats: Residual confounding and reverse causation remain possible in some observational studies, so the main readout is direction and plausibility rather than one exact risk number.
